bounds.domain: One immutable deployment with a complete abstract object set and one pre-existing active deployment; one upload, publication request, retirement request and deletion. Both known and transport-ambiguous SQL outcomes are represented.
bounds.atomicity: The primary database evaluates status guards under its row lock. Publication stores the exact prefix and manifest together. A delayed finalizer cannot publish after acknowledged retirement. The model assumes immutable deployment IDs and complete acknowledged object writes.
bounds.gaps: No general TypeScript refinement, live R2 proof, account deletion or authorization proof, multi-upload version allocation, object integrity proof or general orphan collection. Unacknowledged retirement and deletion retain objects. Existing active content and request admission are assumed valid. The separate app_cleanup_manifest model owns upload plans, writer quiescence and app-delete cleanup. This publication projection retains its original manifest/retirement authority.
bounds.progress: Fair continuation of outstanding storage operations gives a terminal result; success, availability, cleanup after lost receipts and elapsed deadlines are not promised.
bounds.conformance: Ten real PGlite service/repository cases plus five real PostgreSQL cases. Four PG tests observe row-lock wait chains across separate connections; the fifth loses the reply after publication and activation committed. These selected interleavings do not establish general SQL refinement.

assumptions: Outstanding SQL and object-store operations eventually return under weak fairness of finish. This is not a live provider, deadline or successful-publication claim.
